+# The affine partition flag maximum
+
+## Abstract
+
+The flag partition maximizes the squared sizes of affine parts outside the origin.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Affine partitions of the punctured vector space).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), [\operatorname{Fact}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)\right)] \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (parts: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)\right)), (\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{isAffinePartition}\left(p, n, parts\right) = \left((\forall (k: \operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)), ((k \in parts) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{Set}.\operatorname{Nonempty}\left((k: \operatorname{Set}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right))\right)))) \land ((\forall (k: \operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)), ((k \in parts) \Rightarrow (\forall (l: \operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)), ((l \in parts) \Rightarrow ((k \ne l) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{Disjoint}\left((k: \operatorname{Set}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)), (l: \operatorname{Set}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right))\right))))))) \land (\forall (v: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)), ((v \ne (0: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right))) \Leftrightarrow (\exists (k: \operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)), ((k \in parts) \land (v \in (k: \operatorname{Set}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right))))))))\right)))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.isAffinePartition` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A finite family of affine subspaces is an affine partition when every part is nonempty, distinct parts are disjoint, and a vector is nonzero exactly when it belongs to one of the parts. This is the partition condition in the source's stabiliser-operation lemma (lines 986–994).
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The squared-cardinality objective).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), [\operatorname{Fact}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)\right)] \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (parts: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)\right)), (\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{sqSum}\left(p, n, parts\right) = \sum_{k \in parts} (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{card}\left(\operatorname{CoeSort}.\operatorname{coe}\left((k: \operatorname{Set}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right))\right)\right)^{2})))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.sqSum` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+sqSum adds the squares of the cardinalities of the affine parts. It is the quantity appearing in the source's overlap bound (lines 1209–1217).
+
+**Definition 1.3 (A coordinate flag cell).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), [\operatorname{Fact}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)\right)] \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (i: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), (\forall (x: \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)), ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagCell}\left(p, n, i, x\right): \operatorname{Set}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)) = \{v: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right) \mid (\forall (j: \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right)), ((j < i) \Rightarrow (v\left(j\right) = (0: \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right))))) \land (v\left(i\right) = x)\})))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.flagCell` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an index i and a nonzero or zero coordinate value x, flagCell p n i x consists of vectors whose coordinates before i vanish and whose i-th coordinate equals x. It is the affine tail described by the source's first-nonzero-coordinate construction (lines 1219–1232).
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The partition by first nonzero coordinate).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), [\operatorname{Fact}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)\right)] \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagPartition}\left(p, n\right) = \operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{image}\left((\Lambda (a: \operatorname{Prod}\left(\operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right), \operatorname{Subtype}\left((\Lambda (x: \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)) \mapsto x \ne (0: \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)))\right)\right)) \mapsto \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagCell}\left(p, n, \operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{fst}\left(a\right), \operatorname{Subtype}.\operatorname{val}\left(\operatorname{Prod}.\operatorname{snd}\left(a\right)\right)\right)), \operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{univ}\left(\right)\right))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.flagPartition` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+flagPartition is the image of all pairs (i,x) with i in Fin n and x a nonzero element of ZMod p under the flag-cell construction. It encodes the measurement procedure and induced partition in the source (lines 1219–1232).
+
+**Definition 1.5 (The value of the flag partition).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), (\forall (n: \mathbb{N}), (\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagValue}\left(p, n\right) = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{range}\left(n\right)} (\left(p - 1\right) \cdot p^{2 \cdot k})))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.flagValue` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+flagValue p n is the finite sum ∑ₖ₍₀≤k<n₎ (p−1)p^(2k), the squared-cardinality value stated for the flag partition in the source (lines 1233–1237).
+
+**Definition 1.6 (The flag partition maximum conjecture).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), [\operatorname{Fact}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)\right)] \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{isAffinePartition}\left(p, n, \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagPartition}\left(p, n\right)\right)) \land ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{sqSum}\left(p, n, \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagPartition}\left(p, n\right)\right) = \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagValue}\left(p, n\right)) \land (\forall (parts: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)\right)), ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{isAffinePartition}\left(p, n, parts\right)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{sqSum}\left(p, n, parts\right) \le \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagValue}\left(p, n\right))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every prime p and natural n, the flag cells form an affine partition of the nonzero vectors, their squared-cardinality sum is flagValue, and every affine partition has no larger squared-cardinality sum. This is the source's maximising-measurement conjecture under the formal reading that all affine partitions are admitted (lines 1215–1232).
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (The affine partition flag maximum is proved).**
+
+$$\forall (p: \mathbb{N}), [\operatorname{Fact}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)\right)] \forall (n: \mathbb{N}), ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{isAffinePartition}\left(p, n, \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagPartition}\left(p, n\right)\right)) \land ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{sqSum}\left(p, n, \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagPartition}\left(p, n\right)\right) = \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagValue}\left(p, n\right)) \land (\forall (parts: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\operatorname{AffineSubspace}\left(\operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right), \operatorname{Fin}\left(n\right) \to \operatorname{ZMod}\left(p\right)\right)\right)), ((\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{isAffinePartition}\left(p, n, parts\right)) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{sqSum}\left(p, n, parts\right) \le \operatorname{D5}.\operatorname{S3}.\operatorname{Quantum}.\operatorname{Magic}.\operatorname{AffinePartitionFlagMaximum}.\operatorname{flagValue}\left(p, n\right))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/heimendahl-heinrich-gross-2022-affine-partition-flag` (proved) by `D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"heimendahl-heinrich-gross-2022-affine-partition-flag","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Quantum/Magic/AffinePartitionFlagMaximum.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Arne Heimendahl; Markus Heinrich; David Gross (2022). *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*. DOI: [10.1063/5.0085774](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085774). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11651v3>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The proof first identifies the cardinality of every nonempty affine part with p raised to the finrank of its direction, and uses disjointness and coverage to show that the part sizes sum to p^n−1. It then introduces a digit potential formed from the base-p digits of s. Its step, affine, and one-unit identities yield the power inequality p^(2k) plus the potential of s−p^k is at most the potential of s whenever p^k ≤ s. Induction over a finite family of powers of p gives the squared-size bound by the potential of the total size, and induction on n evaluates the potential at p^n−1 as flagValue p n.
+
+The flag-cell center Pi.single i x proves nonemptiness; the least nonzero coordinate of a vector gives the unique flag index, proving disjointness and covering exactly the nonzero vectors. Each cell is the space of extensions of Pi.single i x on the record Finset.Iic i. The general record_extension_card theorem gives its cardinality p^(n−1−i). Summing over i and over the p−1 nonzero coordinate values gives flagValue. Combining these facts with the digit-potential bound proves claim (arXiv TeX lines 1219–1245).
+
+## References
+

+import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.AffineSpace.AffineSubspace.Basic
+import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finiteness
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Field.ZMod
+import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Digits.Defs
+import D5.S0.Diagonal.RecordExtensionCount
+
+/-! Affine partitions of the punctured vector space in the conjecture of Heimendahl,
+Heinrich and Gross, arXiv:2011.11651v3. -/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+noncomputable section
+
+namespace D5.S3.Quantum.Magic.AffinePartitionFlagMaximum
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+/-- Nonempty affine parts, disjoint from one another, covering exactly the nonzero vectors. -/
+def isAffinePartition (p n : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
+    (parts : Finset (AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p))) : Prop :=
+  (∀ k ∈ parts, (k : Set (Fin n → ZMod p)).Nonempty) ∧
+  (∀ k ∈ parts, ∀ l ∈ parts, k ≠ l →
+    Disjoint (k : Set (Fin n → ZMod p)) (l : Set (Fin n → ZMod p))) ∧
+  ∀ v : Fin n → ZMod p, v ≠ 0 ↔ ∃ k ∈ parts, v ∈ k
+
+/-- The objective in the affine partition problem. -/
+def sqSum {p n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
+    (parts : Finset (AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p))) : ℕ :=
+  ∑ k ∈ parts, Nat.card k ^ 2
+
+/-- A coordinate cell with all earlier coordinates zero. -/
+def flagCell (p n : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (i : Fin n) (x : ZMod p) :
+    AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p) where
+  carrier := {v | (∀ j < i, v j = 0) ∧ v i = x}
+  smul_vsub_vadd_mem' c a b d ha hb hd := by
+    constructor
+    · intro j hj
+      change c * (a j - b j) + d j = 0
+      rw [ha.1 j hj, hb.1 j hj, hd.1 j hj]
+      simp
+    · change c * (a i - b i) + d i = x
+      rw [ha.2, hb.2, hd.2]
+      simp
+
+/-- All flag cells with nonzero distinguished coordinate. -/
+def flagPartition (p n : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
+    Finset (AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p)) := by
+  classical
+  exact Finset.univ.image
+    (fun a : Fin n × {x : ZMod p // x ≠ 0} => flagCell p n a.1 a.2.1)
+
+/-- The value of the flag partition, with dimensions in increasing order. -/
+def flagValue (p n : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (p - 1) * p ^ (2 * k)
+
+private def radix (p s : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.ofDigits (p ^ 2) (Nat.digits p s)
+
+private lemma radix_zero (p : ℕ) : radix p 0 = 0 := by
+  change Nat.ofDigits (p ^ 2) (Nat.digits p 0) = 0
+  rw [Nat.digits_zero, Nat.ofDigits_nil]
+
+private lemma radix_step {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (s : ℕ) :
+    radix p s = s % p + p ^ 2 * radix p (s / p) := by
+  by_cases hs : s = 0
+  · subst s
+    simp [radix_zero]
+  · change Nat.ofDigits (p ^ 2) (Nat.digits p s) =
+      s % p + p ^ 2 * Nat.ofDigits (p ^ 2) (Nat.digits p (s / p))
+    rw [Nat.digits_def' (by omega) (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hs), Nat.ofDigits_cons]
+
+private lemma radix_affine {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (q r : ℕ) (hr : r < p) :
+    radix p (p * q + r) = r + p ^ 2 * radix p q := by
+  rw [radix_step hp]
+  simp [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hr, Nat.mul_add_div (show 0 < p by omega),
+    Nat.div_eq_of_lt hr]
+
+private lemma radix_one {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) :
+    1 + radix p (s - 1) ≤ radix p s := by
+  induction s using Nat.strong_induction_on with
+  | h s ih =>
+    have hd := Nat.mod_add_div s p
+    have hrlt := Nat.mod_lt s (show 0 < p by omega)
+    by_cases hr : s % p = 0
+    · have hq : 1 ≤ s / p :=
+        Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd hs (Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero hr)) (by omega)
+      have hi := ih (s / p) (Nat.div_lt_self (by omega) (by omega)) hq
+      have he : s - 1 = p * (s / p - 1) + (p - 1) := by
+        calc
+          s - 1 = p * (s / p) - 1 :=
+            congrArg (fun z : ℕ => z - 1) (by
+              simpa only [hr, zero_add] using hd.symm)
+          _ = p * (s / p - 1) + (p - 1) := by
+            rw [Nat.mul_sub_left_distrib, Nat.mul_one]
+            exact (Nat.sub_add_sub_cancel
+              (by simpa only [Nat.mul_one] using Nat.mul_le_mul_left p hq)
+              (by omega : 1 ≤ p)).symm
+      rw [he, radix_affine hp _ _ (by omega), radix_step hp s, hr, zero_add]
+      have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (p ^ 2) hi
+      have hpp : p ≤ p ^ 2 := Nat.le_self_pow (by decide) p
+      have hpeq := Nat.sub_add_cancel (show 1 ≤ p by omega)
+      nlinarith
+    · have he : s - 1 = p * (s / p) + (s % p - 1) := by
+        calc
+          s - 1 = (p * (s / p) + s % p) - 1 :=
+            congrArg (fun z : ℕ => z - 1) (Nat.div_add_mod s p).symm
+          _ = p * (s / p) + (s % p - 1) :=
+            Nat.add_sub_assoc (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr hr) _
+      rw [he, radix_affine hp _ _ (by omega), radix_step hp s]
+      omega
+
+private lemma radix_power {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (k s : ℕ) (hs : p ^ k ≤ s) :
+    p ^ (2 * k) + radix p (s - p ^ k) ≤ radix p s := by
+  induction k generalizing s with
+  | zero => simpa using radix_one hp s hs
+  | succ k ih =>
+    have hq : p ^ k ≤ s / p :=
+      (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le (show 0 < p by omega)).2 (by simpa [pow_succ] using hs)
+    have he : s - p ^ (k + 1) = p * (s / p - p ^ k) + s % p := by
+      calc
+        s - p ^ (k + 1) = (s % p + p * (s / p)) - p * p ^ k := by
+          rw [pow_succ', Nat.mod_add_div]
+        _ = s % p + (p * (s / p) - p * p ^ k) :=
+          Nat.add_sub_assoc (Nat.mul_le_mul_left p hq) _
+        _ = p * (s / p - p ^ k) + s % p := by
+          rw [← Nat.mul_sub_left_distrib, Nat.add_comm]
+    rw [he, radix_affine hp _ _ (Nat.mod_lt _ (by omega)), radix_step hp s]
+    have hi := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (p ^ 2) (ih (s / p) hq)
+    rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one, pow_add]
+    nlinarith
+
+private lemma power_family_bound {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) {a : Type*}
+    (t : Finset a) (size : a → ℕ) (hs : ∀ x ∈ t, ∃ k, size x = p ^ k) :
+    ∑ x ∈ t, size x ^ 2 ≤ radix p (∑ x ∈ t, size x) := by
+  classical
+  induction t using Finset.induction_on with
+  | empty => simp [radix_zero]
+  | @insert a t ha ih =>
+    have hi := ih (fun x hx => hs x (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hx))
+    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hs a (Finset.mem_insert_self a t)
+    have hpow : size a ^ 2 = p ^ (2 * k) := by
+      rw [hk, ← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm k 2]
+    have hh := radix_power hp k (size a + ∑ x ∈ t, size x) (by omega)
+    rw [← hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel_left] at hh
+    rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha]
+    omega
+
+private lemma radix_value {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (n : ℕ) :
+    radix p (p ^ n - 1) = flagValue p n := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => exact radix_zero p
+  | succ n ih =>
+    have he : p ^ (n + 1) - 1 = p * (p ^ n - 1) + (p - 1) := by
+      rw [pow_succ', Nat.mul_sub_left_distrib, Nat.mul_one]
+      exact (Nat.sub_add_sub_cancel (a := p * p ^ n) (b := p) (c := 1)
+        (by simpa only [Nat.mul_one] using
+          Nat.mul_le_mul_left p (Nat.one_le_pow n p (by omega))) (by omega)).symm

+    (parts : Finset (AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p)))

+    ∑ k ∈ parts, Nat.card k = p ^ n - 1 := by

+  let f := fun k : AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p) => (k : Set (Fin n → ZMod p)).toFinset
+  have hd : (parts : Set _).PairwiseDisjoint f := by
+    intro k hk l hl hkl

+    simpa [f] using (hparts.2.2 v).symm

+      intro k hk

+  classical

+      constructor
+      · intro hv j hj

+        · simpa [Pi.single_eq_of_ne (ne_of_lt hj)] using hv.1 j hj
+        · simpa using hv.2
+      · intro hv
+        constructor
+        · intro j hj

+  simp only [ZMod.card, Fintype.card_fin, Fin.card_Iic]
+  congr 1
+  omega

+    (Pi.single i x : Fin n → ZMod p) ∈ flagCell p n i x := by
+  constructor
+  · intro j hj
+    simp [Pi.single_eq_of_ne (ne_of_lt hj)]
+  · simp

+private lemma flag_indices_of_mem {p n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
+    (a b : Fin n × {x : ZMod p // x ≠ 0}) (v : Fin n → ZMod p)
+    (ha : v ∈ flagCell p n a.1 a.2.1) (hb : v ∈ flagCell p n b.1 b.2.1) : a = b := by
+  have hi : a.1 = b.1 := by
+    apply le_antisymm
+    · by_contra h
+      exact b.2.2 (hb.2.symm.trans (ha.1 b.1 (lt_of_not_ge h)))
+    · by_contra h
+      exact a.2.2 (ha.2.symm.trans (hb.1 a.1 (lt_of_not_ge h)))
+  apply Prod.ext hi
+  apply Subtype.ext
+  exact ha.2.symm.trans (by simpa [hi] using hb.2)

+  intro a b hab
+  apply flag_indices_of_mem a b (Pi.single a.1 a.2.1) (flag_center _ _)
+  change flagCell p n a.1 a.2.1 = flagCell p n b.1 b.2.1 at hab
+  rw [← hab]
+  exact flag_center _ _

+  · intro k hk
+    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hk
+    exact ⟨_, flag_center a.1 a.2.1⟩
+  · intro k hk l hl hkl
+    obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hk
+    obtain ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hl
+    apply Set.disjoint_left.mpr
+    intro v hva hvb
+    exact hkl (congrArg (fun a => flagCell p n a.1 a.2.1)
+      (flag_indices_of_mem a b v hva hvb))
+  · intro v
+    constructor
+    · intro hv
+      have hex : ∃ j : Fin n, v j ≠ 0 := Function.ne_iff.mp hv
+      let nz := Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin n => v j ≠ 0)
+      have hnz : nz.Nonempty := by
+        simpa only [nz, Finset.filter_nonempty_iff, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] using hex
+      let i := nz.min' hnz
+      have hi : v i ≠ 0 := (Finset.mem_filter.mp (Finset.min'_mem nz hnz)).2
+      refine ⟨flagCell p n i (v i), ?_, ?_⟩
+      · exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, ⟨v i, hi⟩), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
+      · refine ⟨?_, rfl⟩
+        intro j hj
+        by_contra hzero
+        have hle : i ≤ j := Finset.min'_le nz j (by simp [nz, hzero])
+        exact not_le_of_gt hj hle
+    · rintro ⟨k, hk, hv⟩ hzero
+      obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hk
+      exact a.2.2 (hv.2.symm.trans (by simp [hzero]))

+private lemma flag_sum {p n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] :
+    sqSum (flagPartition p n) = flagValue p n := by
+  classical
+  change (∑ k ∈ Finset.univ.image
+    (fun a : Fin n × {x : ZMod p // x ≠ 0} => flagCell p n a.1 a.2.1),
+      Nat.card k ^ 2) = flagValue p n
+  rw [Finset.sum_image (fun a _ b _ h => flag_index_injective h)]
+  simp_rw [flag_cell_card]
+  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+  have hc : Fintype.card {x : ZMod p // x ≠ 0} = p - 1 := by
+    simp [Fintype.card_subtype_compl]
+  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, hc, smul_eq_mul]
+  rw [Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun i : ℕ => (p - 1) * (p ^ (n - 1 - i)) ^ 2)]
+  change (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (p - 1) * (p ^ (n - 1 - i)) ^ 2) = _
+  simp_rw [← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm _ 2]
+  exact Finset.sum_range_reflect (fun k => (p - 1) * p ^ (2 * k)) n
+
+private lemma partition_bound {p n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
+    (parts : Finset (AffineSubspace (ZMod p) (Fin n → ZMod p)))
+    (hparts : isAffinePartition p n parts) : sqSum parts ≤ flagValue p n := by
+  have hp : 2 ≤ p := (Fact.out : p.Prime).two_le
+  have h := power_family_bound hp parts (fun k => Nat.card k)
+    (fun k hk => ⟨_, affine_card k (hparts.1 k hk)⟩)
+  rw [partition_card parts hparts, radix_value hp] at h
+  exact h
+
+/-- The flag partition attains the maximum over every affine partition of the punctured space. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (n : ℕ),
+    isAffinePartition p n (flagPartition p n) ∧
+    sqSum (flagPartition p n) = flagValue p n ∧
+    ∀ parts, isAffinePartition p n parts → sqSum parts ≤ flagValue p n
+
+/-- The affine partition flag maximum conjecture. -/
+theorem result : claim := by
+  intro p hp n
+  exact ⟨flag_partition, flag_sum, fun parts hparts => partition_bound parts hparts⟩
+
+end D5.S3.Quantum.Magic.AffinePartitionFlagMaximum

+# Heimendahl, Heinrich and Gross, The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide
+
+A. Heimendahl, M. Heinrich and D. Gross, Journal of Mathematical Physics 63(11) (2022) 112201, DOI 10.1063/5.0085774; arXiv:2011.11651v3. Quotations are from the arXiv v3 TeX source.
+
+For prime $d$, the paper writes the stabiliser operations in the diagonal subpolytope through states $\sigma=\frac1{d^n-1}\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|\,|s_K\rangle\langle s_K|$, where $\mathcal K$ is a disjoint partition of $\mathbb F_d^n\setminus0$ by affine spaces. It bounds $\langle+|\sigma|+\rangle\le\frac1{d^n(d^n-1)}\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|^2$ and conjectures:
+
+> We conjecture that such a projective measurement which maximizes \eqref{eq:estimation-of-overlapII} has the following form
+
+namely measuring the qudits in turn in the computational basis until a nonzero outcome occurs. The induced partition consists of the sets of vectors with a given first nonzero coordinate and value; with coordinates indexed from $0$, the cell whose first nonzero coordinate is $i$ has $n-1-i$ free coordinates. The paper writes the cells as $xe_i+(0^i\oplus\mathbb F_d^{n-i})$ with $|K|=d^{n-i}$ for $i=0,\dots,n-1$, which counts one free coordinate too many; its sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(d-1)d^{2k}$ matches the cells of the measurement procedure. The paper evaluates the resulting sum $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(d-1)d^{2k}$ as $(d-1)\frac{d^{2n-2}}{d^2-1}$; the sum equals $\frac{d^{2n}-1}{d+1}$.

+# The flag partition maximizes the squared sizes of affine parts outside the origin
+
+## Problem
+
+A. Heimendahl, M. Heinrich and D. Gross, *The axiomatic and the operational approaches to resource theories of magic do not coincide*, arXiv:2011.11651v3 (J. Math. Phys. 63, 112201, 2022), conjecture in the remark following Corollary `cor:SO-cap-AD`. The checked TeX member `paper_new.tex`, lines 1219–1227, reads:
+
+> We conjecture that such a projective measurement which maximizes \eqref{eq:estimation-of-overlapII}
+> has the following form:
+>
+> Measure the first qudit in the computational basis.
+>
+> If $ x \neq 0 $ is measured, do nothing.
+> If $ 0 $ is measured, measure the second qudit in the computational basis.
+> Continue in this fashion until all qubits are measured.
+>
+> If $ 0 $ has been measured on every qudit, apply a Hadamard gate to every qudit.
+
+Write $p$ for the source's prime dimension $d$, and $V=\mathbb F_p^n$, represented by `Fin n → ZMod p`. An affine partition (`isAffinePartition`) is a finite set of nonempty affine subspaces, with distinct parts disjoint, such that a vector belongs to a part if and only if it is nonzero. Its objective is `sqSum`, namely $\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|^2$.
+
+The cells $K_{i,x}=\{v\in V:(\forall j<i,\ v_j=0),\ v_i=x\}$, for $0\le i<n$ and $x\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{0\}$, form `flagPartition p n`. Put $S_p(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(p-1)p^{2k}$, the definition `flagValue p n`.
+
+Issue [#25329](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/25329) fixes the reading: for every prime $p$ and every $n\in\mathbb N$, the flag family is an affine partition, its objective equals $S_p(n)$, and every affine partition of $V\setminus\{0\}$ has objective at most $S_p(n)$. This is the proposition `claim`, proved by `result`.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The source compares stabiliser operations (SO), defined by Clifford gates, Pauli measurements and classical control, with completely stabiliser-preserving channels (CSP). Lemma `lem:so-in-ad` (TeX lines 986–994) expresses the relevant SO states through affine partitions of the nonzero vectors. Equation `eq:estimation-of-overlapII` (lines 1215–1217) bounds their overlap by $\langle+|\sigma|+\rangle\le\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|^2/[p^n(p^n-1)]$. Maximizing the squared-size sum therefore supplies a quantitative upper bound for that comparison when $n\ge1$. The source's permitted partitions have additional tree structure; the formal statement bounds all affine partitions.
+
+## Gap
+
+The bounded literature check recorded in #25329 is attributed there to the orchestrator (Claude Code, Opus):
+
+- The arXiv v3 source contains the conjecture; the journal text was not read.
+- Citation-context and affine-subspace searches in arXiv:2311.06133, 2507.10851, 2610.38401, 2211.15678, 2202.07867, 2507.11793 and 2608.10202 found no settlement of this conjecture or bound on the squared-size sum.
+- Zenodo, GitHub preregistration and repository searches found no existing settlement in their searched scope.
+
+`not-found-in-searched-scope`. These searches do not establish worldwide novelty or priority.
+
+## Route
+
+The helper names below refer to private lemmas in the canonical module.
+
+1. **Part cardinalities.** For prime $p$, natural $n$ and a nonempty affine subspace $K\subseteq\mathbb F_p^n$, `affine_card` gives $|K|=p^{\dim K.direction}$. For a finite family satisfying `isAffinePartition p n parts`, `partition_card` gives $\sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|=p^n-1$.
+2. **Radix potential.** Define $h_p(s)$ by reading the base-$p$ digits of $s$ as base-$p^2$ digits (`radix`). For natural $p\ge2$ and natural $k,s$ with $p^k\le s$, `radix_power` gives $p^{2k}+h_p(s-p^k)\le h_p(s)$. For any type, finite index set $t$ and size function into $\mathbb N$ such that every indexed size is $p^k$ for some natural $k$, `power_family_bound`, assuming $p\ge2$, gives $\sum_{x\in t}size(x)^2\le h_p(\sum_{x\in t}size(x))$. For $p\ge2$ and every natural $n$, `radix_value` evaluates $h_p(p^n-1)=S_p(n)$. For prime $p$, natural $n$ and `isAffinePartition p n parts`, `partition_bound` combines these facts to bound `sqSum parts` by `flagValue p n`.
+3. **Attainment.** For prime $p$, natural $n$, $i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and any $x\in\mathbb F_p$, including zero, `flag_cell_card` gives $|K_{i,x}|=p^{n-1-i}$. For prime $p$ and every natural $n$, `flag_partition` proves that the cells with $x\ne0$ form an affine partition, and `flag_sum` proves that their objective equals $S_p(n)$. Together with `partition_bound`, these are the three conjuncts of `claim`.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+The settlement would miss the source's question if the objective or admissible cells differed. The formal cells follow the measurement procedure: coordinates before the first nonzero outcome are fixed to zero, that outcome is fixed, and the remaining coordinates are free. With zero-based $i$, there are $n-1-i$ free coordinates. The source's display at TeX lines 1230–1232 instead uses $n-i$; its displayed affine set at $i=0$ would be the whole space and contain zero. The formal reading follows the procedure, not that inconsistent display. The prime-field scope follows the source's setup at lines 131–133; the isolated $\mathbb F_2^n$ in line 1218 does not restrict `claim` to qubits.
+
+Bounding every affine partition also bounds the tree-structured subclass described by the source. Identifying the proposed procedure with a permissible stabiliser operation is a source-level bridge, not a Lean statement of this module. Neither quantum-state normalization nor attainment of the overlap bound is formalized here. The case $n=0$ is included in `claim` as an empty partition with objective zero; the overlap expression is used only for $n\ge1$, when its denominator is positive.
+

+

+
+Tier 1 conjecture of a 2020 preprint published in 2022, checked in arXiv v3, preregistered in issue #25329 before any Lean.
+`theorem`; resolution `proved`.
+
+The module is admitted under the open-problem-resolution basis of CLAUDE.md §3.2; the per-declaration proof shapes are listed in the delivery PR. There is no digestion atom.
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+**Proved by `result`:** for every prime $p$ and every natural $n$, `flagPartition p n` is a finite partition of $\mathbb F_p^n\setminus\{0\}$ into nonempty, pairwise disjoint affine subspaces, its squared-cardinality sum equals $S_p(n)$, and every such affine partition has squared-cardinality sum at most $S_p(n)$.
+
+**Computed, not formalized:** None.
+
+**Argued, not formalized.**
+
+- *Cardinality mechanism and equality profiles.* For any integer base $b\ge2$, consider a finite multiset of powers $b^j$ with total $b^n-1$, for natural $n$. Replacing $b$ copies of $b^j$ by one copy of $b^{j+1}$ preserves the total and increases the squared-size sum by $(b^2-b)b^{2j}>0$. Repeating terminates because the number of parts decreases. The final multiplicities are the base-$b$ digits of $b^n-1$: $b-1$ at each exponent below $n$, and zero elsewhere. Thus a maximizing size multiset has precisely that profile. This argument concerns cardinalities; the replacements need not be realizable as mergers of affine parts.
+- *Extension and geometric sharpness.* The same cardinality argument applies over any finite field of size $q$, since each nonempty affine part has $q^r$ points and the punctured space has $q^n-1$ points; the coordinate flag cells provide $q-1$ parts of each size $q^j$ for $0\le j<n$. This extension beyond prime fields is not a statement of `result`. An invertible linear change of coordinates preserves affine parts, disjointness, the punctured space and cardinalities, so it preserves the maximum. A classification of all maximizing partitions, and whether every maximizer arises from a complete flag, remain open here.
+- *Corrected arithmetic.* The source writes "$\sum_{K \in \mathcal{K}} |K|^2 = \sum_{k = 0}^{n-1}  (d-1) d^{2k} = (d-1) \frac{d^{2n-2}}{d^2-1}$" (TeX line 1235). For $p\ge2$ and natural $n$, telescoping gives $(p^2-1)\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p^{2k}=p^{2n}-1$, hence $S_p(n)=(p^{2n}-1)/(p+1)$. For $n\ge1$, its normalized value is $S_p(n)/[p^n(p^n-1)]=(p^n+1)/[(p+1)p^n]$, tending to $1/(p+1)$ as $n$ grows with $p$ fixed. This corrects the source's "$\approx \frac{1}{d^3}$" at line 1241. The closed form and limit are not part of the Lean type of `result`.
+- *Effect on the source's separation claim.* For prime $p$ and $n\ge2$, the corrected normalized value is at most $(p^2+1)/[(p+1)p^2]$, which is below $1/p$ by $(p-1)/[(p+1)p^2]>0$. Combining the partition bound with the source's overlap inequality therefore gives a positive separation uniform in $n\ge2$ under the source's state representation. At $n=1$ the normalized value equals $1/p$. This supplies the quantitative consequence sought in the conjectural remark for $n\ge2$, with corrected arithmetic. Corollary `cor:SO-cap-AD` already has an independent strict-inequality argument at lines 1197–1207. Neither that corollary, the SO/CSP channel representations, nor overlap attainment is proved by this module; no other source result is settled by `result`.
+
+## ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED
+
+The literature check is bounded by the searches reported in #25329; its seven citing-work readings, Semantic Scholar citation listing and Zenodo/GitHub search results were not independently reproduced. The journal text was not read, so retention of the conjecture and its displayed arithmetic in the journal version is unverified. The arXiv v3 TeX conjecture, surrounding partition lemma and quantitative remark were read directly.

+The arguments under "Argued, not formalized" are not Lean conclusions of this module, including the equality-profile characterization, arbitrary finite-field extension, closed-form evaluation, asymptotic value and conditional quantum separation. The correspondence between source-admissible operations and partitions, the source's quantum overlap inequality, overlap attainment and classification of maximizing geometries are outside the formal statement; the last two remain open here.
